The decisive question as we will see from now on is whether the Belgrade government actually exercised such a degree of control in all fields, I emphasise that, as to justify treating the Bosnian Serbs as acting on behalf of the Belgrade government. The wordings I use are the wordings from the International Court of Justice in the Nicaragua case. Of course I changed the "Nicaraguans" to "Bosnians". So the issue is not whether the army of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the VRS, used equipment and armament that used to belong to the JNA or that a former JNA official continue their duty in the VRS, but whether this army acted as an organ or an agent of the federal government of the Federal Republic in Belgrade. That would require actually exercising a degree of control in all fields, as I just explained to you. In the Nicaragua case the International Court of Justice, and we are using the same authority, both the Prosecution and the Defence, the International Court of Justice had to determine whether or not the relationship of the Contras to the United States government was so much one of dependence on the one side and control at the other, I also emphasise that because I have heard a lot on dependence and I have heard not very much of control ----

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: You keep referring to agent or organ.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Organ or agent, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Does that wording come from the Nicaragua case? Is the criterion?

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: It is the same wording as you find in the Appeals Chamber decision and in the Nicaragua case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: So that is the criterion?

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but then they work it out in the Nicaragua case by saying such a degree of control, etc., etc.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: I do not understand how that equates agent or organ?

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: But that is ----

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: It is all a question of degree of control, is it? I mean there is a great difference between being an organ of something and being an agent.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think they mainly thought of being an agent and then you especially need this level of control, this degree of control. I do not think -- well, at least in my opinion, it is not a matter of being an organ, but rather of whether or not they were acting as agents.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Orie, I think we know what Nicaragua held, but do you not see a difference though? First of all, we are not talking about state responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: I will come to that later, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: But let me talk about other factual differences. You do not have the same identity of ethnicity, as you have already admitted, between Americans, most Americans, or the United States of America and the Contras. You do not have the same goals, ideological goals between the United States and the Contras, but you do have that kind of relationship between Bosnian Serbs and Serbs from the Federal Republic. You do not -- I was getting ready to say you did not have the presence of the army in the United States Army in Nicaragua, but I think I will pass on that. But there are some differences, are there not?

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, there are some differences, your Honour. I will come to what exactly there was of the United States in Nicaragua later. If you say, well, they are not of the same ethnic background, would that actually that mean if you have common political aspirations with someone who is of a different ethnic background, that then it would not create state responsibility, and if it is of people of the same ethnic background that then you would be responsible for it?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: No, I am not saying you have to have the similarity of the ethnicity. I am pointing out the absence of what I consider to be important differences. I do not think the Contras in the United States were trying to join together as one state. I do not think United States was particularly interested in having Nicaragua. I do not know. Nicaragua, I do not know, was particularly interested in becoming a part of the United States. But I see a lot of factual differences.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: At the time of the history I think that the Bosnian Republic first of all wanted to be independent from Sarajevo, and whether they would like to join Serbia proper later that also came in a later stage in the history. Of course, I do agree with you that there must have been some common goal between the Contras and the US, because otherwise I could hardly imagine why they did, as I will explain to you, what the United States government. Let me first continue because ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We need to adjourn at 6.00. Do you want to wrap up now or would you like to begin again, I do not mean at the beginning but begin at this phrase?

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: I will tomorrow summarise in three lines what I have said today and then continue.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good. Tomorrow we are going to begin at 9 o'clock and will go from 9.00 until 1.00. If we are not able to complete, then we will then continue on Friday afternoon, it will be in the afternoon but at a time to be determined. So we will adjourn until 9 o'clock tomorrow. 6.00 p.m. (The court adjourned until the following day). 26 27 28
